name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Game of the Year Edition (2009)

data: Amazing game, the World Building Is Top Notch, the story is fun and engaging, 10/10 would recommend
the graphics are pretty good ) this game is a great, great game
It's a great game and even better with mods
The story is amazing, the world is amazing, the soundtrack is amazing, the character progression and creation are amazing, and the gameplay blew me away
This is well worth the price
This game crashes so much it's virtually unplayable
They look terrible to a point where it's hard to take the characters and what they say seriously
The combat system in this game sucks because the stamina dictates too much and there's no sprint button that standarizes movement

If you purchase the Game of the Year Edition, you will NOT be able to purchase the Deluxe edition, and you will have NO WAY to acquire the rest of the DLC. The Steam store will show that you own the Deluxe edition (even though you don't) and so you will not be able to purchase it. There is also no upgrade feature, and Steam support WILL NOT refund you if you have played for more than 2 hours.

The Deluxe Edution is worth your purchase, but please watch out for this issue. I have never encountered an issue like this with any other game on Steam. It is so dissapointing and frustrating that I have NO WAY of acquiring the rest of the DLC.

This game is just awesome. There's little else to say about it. It is an enormous world full of quests to complete, orders to join and advance in, spells to invent, items to enchant, monsters to slay, people to meet... There's so much to do you that the gameplay is timeless! I actually had this game in high school, and after playing it so much I realized "I think I'm done. Nothing sounds appealing to me on this game anymore." A few years later, and it's like a brand-new experience all over again. Seriously. Invest the money to buy this if you want an AMAZING RPG.

A game that I come back to time after time after time. Great game with absolutely limitless possibilities, especially the PC/Steam version and the mind boggling huge assortment of different mods. Play it now and get pumped for Skyrim in November! Personally I'm trying to run all the dungeons in the game prior to Skyrim comining out while playing with OOO. Hopefully I can make it. :)
Have hundreds of hours outside of steam. Overall, it's worth your time. I will say that you probably need to look into how to level your character properly though.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion was my first game into the world of Bethesda's Legendary World of RPG gaming. The stories of the Main Quest, Mages Guild, Fighters Guild are my favorites as the Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood are exciting.

My first experience with this game goes back to the PS3 Game of the Year edition and I would play it non-stop and I still do on both PS3 and PC. I hope all of you find this game as exciting as I do. Of course, I pay more attention to the story than that of the gameplay mechanics.

One of those games that's so special, and has that "finished" feel. There are endless little sidequests and secrets to find, countless dungeons that you will not find everything on your 1st, 2nd or even 3rd playthrough. Become a master magician with custom spells, a fleet footed archer or even a master acrobat and jump over buildings.

Don't bother with inferior "remasters" that cover everything in unreal slop whilst worsening the balance in ALL aspects imaginable. Just learn basic math. There is no such thing as "Overleveling" unless you just binged alchemy for 50 skill level ups. 55€ in order to do like one third less damage with a Claymore weighing 70 pounds compared to a damn dagger because they had to make a two-handed weapon swing like you're in world of warcraft.

An amazing chapter of an awesome series! Would recommend waiting for a sale to grab this one, I managed to get it for less than $5. It IS possible to mod the Steam version, and is quite easy with Nexus Mod Manager or Oblivion Mod Manager. It may look a little out of date, but with ENB mods it can look quite pretty.

10/10 easily, although Steam Workshop and Achievements would be nice, although it's a little late to be asking for them, but you can always hope I suppose...

The combat system within this game is lacking for modern standards and is very difficult to adapt to from modern standards. There is not clear instructions for the game and it is very difficult to get into this game due a poor way the game presents the plot.
But!!!
There is some potential in this game due to the good story line. It maybe suggestible that you buy this game, for the story alone but If you are looking for an RPG and have fallen in love with the elder scrolls series just be aware this game is difficult to adapt to mainly due to the UI being the most lacking. I suggest modding this game to make it play well and fall in with modern standards.
Given the date of which this game is made in it receives a a :) from me but you really need to be aware that the UI is extremely lacking and makes it difficult to play.
old but gold, this is MUCH better than the so called "remastered" version made with UE5 slop. it has high quality in every way possible and is super fun unlike the remastered version.

Other than some nigling issues players have with the mechanics, how creatures level up with you so you never really feel challenged, I think the only reason this game gets so much flack is that the setting never really stood out. Yes Morrowind was a great game with a unique setting, but Oblivion, even with it's typical "High Fantasy" Medeival setting that's been done to death so many other times, is still a great game. I logged countless hours on this game when it first came out for the 360 and my only complaint then was that there was so much to do and see, I couldn't finish it so I could trade it in and try a new game! That is not really a complaint though, because I enjoyed every second I played this game, and I still do, and I'm still discovering new things every time I play it.

Elder Scrolls IV Oblivion is open world RPG set in classic fantasy setting. After completing tutorial section, you can travel anywhere in the game world, create your own adventure and ignore or postpone the main storyline quests as long as you want it to. Guilds are, hands down, the best part of TES IV Oblivon. On the other hand, oblivon gates, caves, forts and ruins are bland and boring. Overall, Elder Scrolls IV Oblivion is enjoyable power fantasy game and "radiant" NPC augment whole gameplay experience to an envious level.

One of the best stories in a video game.
Some times not all that fun to play due to asset fatigue, but one of the most iconic stories to be told.

This is genuinely a masterpiece, if you don't like it, its because you don't have powerful nostalgia backing you up. Its not about the graphics, the weird AI, or the bugs, its about playing a game back when they weren't the most technologically advanced as they are now. Its about playing a game with some of the most interesting gameplay, quests and RPG elements. This game has soul and if you can't see then I truly pity you. This game was a great part of my childhood and now its a great part of my adulthood.

I love this game so much!
The characters are so memorable and engaging.
The plot is long and winding in a way that kept me thinking for a while.
There are so many places to explore and hundreds of side quests for you to find.

Oblivion was an important game in my life. I started playing it when would visit my dad's house. Randomly getting a remaster makes me feel like I was playing a demo all my life. But at least in the demo starlight worked. Give me back my dup'ing glitch! The arena lantern should bounce!

You've never played a game until you've played Oblivion. This is most likely one of my favorite games. I've spent countless hours on PC and console playing this game taking all I could out of it, and I'm still not finished. This game is a complete masterpiece and will definitely never disappoint.

I played about a thousand hours before this came out on Steam. The questlines and world building is excellent; the leveling system is counter intuitive but you have plenty of unofficial mods to address this issue - or you can just drop the difficulty and don't think too much about it.
Classic Elder Scrolls' games are always great to jump into again. Take some time to jump in to Tamriel and close shut the jaws of Oblivion
Best Elder Scrolls game! This is what made me fall in love with the franchise. Game of the Year Edition is necessary! The Shivering Isles DLC is the best I've played of any game.

My favourite TES game! A classic fantasy RPG but with enough modern mojo (for 2006 anyway) to not be frustrating. The Jeremy Soule soundtrack is naturally fantastic, and despite its age the environments don't look bad at all, it's just the character models that look goofy but that just adds to the unique Oblivion experience! The only negative I will say is Oblivion Gates are repetitive and a pain, but they are optional so it's no big deal. There is also no escaping that it is a dated game but this is eclipsed by how fun the RPG mechanics and quests are.

So far actually amazing and in my opinion looks fantastic! First time playing and I recommend it 100% Really fun (I grew up playing skyrim and honestly kicking myself in the ass for not playing this game sooner). Ended up beating the game on my xbox 360 to really recapture that childhood feel of TES and man.... It was beautiful currently replaying it on the remaster and it still has that same charm.
Amazing game o7

I do recommend this game, and here is a quick rundown on why.

I played this game a few years after it came out, on a machine that was woefully underpowered for it. I actually burnt out my graphics card on this game, and had to do without a PC for two years. During the time I played it, the FPS could be described as "glacial" but I still played it. Playing this game on a computer that was not good enough to run it, was better than not playing it at all. It also taught me that 30FPS, is really not nearly as bad as most people make it out to be, especially when you killed your PC playing oblivion at less than 10 frames per second.
one of the best rpgs i ever play and this one got me into rpg games so buy it or skyrim :D
Oblivion is another really fun game that I like, and you should definatly give it a try if you haven't played it before.

While i love the game itself do keep in mind that the Game of the Year Edition doesn't include all DLC and that you can't buy them separetely or upgrade to the Deluxe edition. Your only option is to buy the game again and you won't be refunded by buying it twice.

So if you want to buy this but the Deluxe version.

What can be said about Oblivion? Well here's telling you why...

Pros:
- Fantastic soundtrack
- Fun quests (Dark Brotherhood is probably the best)
- A lot of replay value
- Memorable NPCs (Like the Adoring Fan)
- Mods
- Combat

Cons:
- Leveling system (Sleeping in a bed and leveling up)
- Ugly as hell NPCs
- Voice acting is a bit cringey and every race sounds the same

If you can get over the cons, You got yourself an awesome RPG.
10/10
As the very first TES game I ever played, Oblivion holds a special place in my little antisocial heart. With all of the various story lines to play through, TES4 will keep you busy for DAYS!

Always love games that let me do my own thing.

Oblivion provides that in spades.
One of the best games ever made. Just because its older doesn't mean that it is bad. Everyone should play and beat this game at least once in their life.
They game has an amazing main story with a good magic system and the dlc are equally as captivating over all one of my favorite games and great for the time frame it was produced

If you have only played Morrowind or Skyrim, you should give this one a try.
The mechanics are a nice balance between the traditional implemented in Morrowind and the more casual mechanics of Skyrim.

I would highly recommend some mods for textures and faces because they are kinda aged.

I have to give a negative review after many years. I purchased the original iteration of the GOTY edition which included all of the downloadable content, but coming back to play after some time I find that they have removed the add-on dlc from the GOTY edition leaving just Shivering Isles and Knights of the Nine and now they are requiring me to purchase the GOTY Deluxe edition to regain access to content that I have already purchased.

i got this cause i liked the memes "and i have not play a elder scrolls game don't boo me" under a hour in and i already got lost that's fine the ruin was okay i got the game of the year edition cause you know it is clearly better it was challenging already and i love those type of games the goblins are too strong and the start and the boss happy 25th birthday elder scrolls
i give it a 4.5 out of 5!!
really fun game and its aged pretty well imo all the clunkiness just adds to the game
A timeless classic that I'm always happy to return to because of the story and the open world, which is still fun even after 17 years and can still surprise and draw me in.

good story as always

but skyrim is the best by far

have a good oblivion

I may not have many hours on this game for the PC but let me tell you, I spent my entire Jr high years and high school years playing this game non stop since release.

I owe this game so much. It allowed me to lose my virginity. No way I would have lost it without this game. Before this game i was just a weak minded fool. Once I started this game, i felt my body and my mind ascending. I can feel the soul of this game combining with mine. I became one with the game.

My family thought they lost me once i started wearing full suits of armor but i knew it had to be done. I won my wife's heart with this armor. Without it she would have never seen me. I owe this game my first born and it shall receive it.

Forever this game will stay in my heart.
14 years old and still this game holds up the story, the world it's very beautiful and the DLC content? specifically the shivering isle? magnificent I would highly recommend this game to everyone

I didn't have a good computer growing up.
I had a friend who did.
I literally went to his house every day to play this game.
I played Oblivion while he sat a few feet from me playing Smash Bros Melee on Gamecube.
I had so much fun and then I would come home to my potato computer with 256 RAM.
Good times.

The best part of this game was the character creation options. It seems to be some sort of downs syndrome simulator. Sometimes i wonder if maybe the world of elder scrolls is really just housed in the imagination of a person with downs syndrome.
Also, there are no dragons. Which is cool i guess.

This time it is Oblivion. Best game ever made in my opinion but give this game to a kid in the new generation and its a dated game with some redeeming qualities. for me this game encorporated my entire life for about 4 years i went between this and modern warfare 2 and talking to my friends at school in party chat and staying up smoking cigs away from our parents playing videogames 11/10 nostalgic fix found

Best Elder Scrolls game IMO. Incredible game, great characters, epic main story, fantastic side quests and a whole lot to do. Put hundreds of hours into this back on Xbox 360 back in the day when it first releaased

Ah Oblivion! THE game that got me into Elder Scrolls because my friend had it on 360 and consequently i started living in his house. Of course i went into Skyrim after, but Oblivion will always be my genesis. So imagine my delight to find it on Steam! This was quickly dashed however by the lack of controller support, which Remastered has addressed now, thankfully! So as much as i love this game, i will never play it for that sole reason.. However! the game itself is great! If keyboard controls are not of concern to you, you will be entertained.

Unlike it's lame cousin Morrowind, you'll enjoy such lovely content as

-premium horse armor
-the opportunity to loot daedric armor from everyone because everything is wearing it (even horses)
-50 oblivion gates with 5 different layouts between them!
-an authentic playtester experience, you'll be bugsolving like a pro in notime
-captain picard shows up with worf or something

What's that? You say you're already buying it as we speak?

CAPITAL!
If once you get into the game it's just one blank color, try turning off HDR. If that doesn't work (like it didn't for me), swap shader packages 2 and 19, immediatly fixed my issue.

A beautiful, immersive classic. Of course everyone has heard of Skyrim, but Oblivion involves you in a far more open, beautiful and medieval world. If you are looking for an extremely fun game with great replayability, I immensely recommend this one.

I spent countless hours when this first came out on my Xbox 360 back in 2006, and enjoyed every moment of it. Going on 8 years later, decided to pick Oblivion up on a Steam Sale for a generous price to play the main story again, and just by doing the main quest line gave me 24 hours of nostalgic fun.

Also adding new mods made it a brand new experience in itself with better graphics, and there's plenty more new content with mods if you feel like devoting more of your time to this legendary RPG.

It's not secret that I love The Elderscrolls Series. This one is great and comes with both expansions. I actually preferred it slightly more than Skyrim. There are tons of user mods out there too that will greatly improve the graphics if you want something a little more modern looking.
Oblivion wasn't perfect but it was much better than Morrowind, regardless of what pretentious gamers will say.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (95%): players praise the story and characters, and many also like the graphics and art.
Bugs and crashes are the main complaint, ahead of story and gameplay complaints.

details.text: For buyers now, recent reviews sit at 88% positive, a small dip from the all-time score.
Players with under 2 hours are less positive than those with over 50 hours, at 83% against 97%.
